response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT DISTINCT team_id FROM team), s AS (SELECT t.team_id, AVG(1.0 * mh.w / NULLIF(mh.g, 0)) AS avg_wr, COUNT(mh.team_id) AS cnt FROM t LEFT JOIN manager_half mh ON mh.team_id = t.team_id GROUP BY t.team_id), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wr) AS mean_wr FROM s) SELECT s.team_id, s.avg_wr, s.cnt, s.avg_wr - m.mean_wr AS diff FROM s CROSS JOIN m WHERE m.mean_wr IS NOT NULL ORDER BY diff DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: A 'team' is identified by team_id, so all seasons of a team_id are pooled. The output only shows team_id, which supports this.
A record with g = 0 has no defined win rate. It is treated as missing for the average but still counted in the record count.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat each row of the team table (year, team_id) as a separate team. Match manager_half on both year and team_id, and show year with team_id.
alternatives.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT t.year, t.team_id, AVG(1.0 * mh.w / NULLIF(mh.g, 0)) AS avg_wr, COUNT(mh.team_id) AS cnt FROM team t LEFT JOIN manager_half mh ON mh.team_id = t.team_id AND mh.year = t.year GROUP BY t.year, t.team_id), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wr) AS mean_wr FROM s) SELECT s.year, s.team_id, s.avg_wr, s.cnt, s.avg_wr - m.mean_wr AS diff FROM s CROSS JOIN m WHERE m.mean_wr IS NOT NULL ORDER BY diff DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10
